issues.t: Takata passenger airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can notice. The danger only shows up in a crash, when the passenger front airbag goes off.
issues.why: The SC 430's front passenger airbag used a Takata inflator whose propellant breaks down over years of heat and humidity. When it fires it can burst and throw metal pieces into the cabin. Some replacement inflators fitted under the first recalls were the same design and were recalled again.
issues.next: Check your VIN at a Lexus dealer or on nhtsa.gov/recalls. If any airbag recall is open, book the free repair right away and keep anyone out of the passenger seat until it is done.

issues.t: Retractable hardtop stops partway or won't close
issues.sym: The folding roof stops part way, won't close at all, or closes but the warning light and chime stay on. The trunk may refuse to open and the rear side windows may not go back up.
issues.why: The roof is run by several small computers, limit switches and hinges. A hinge that has moved out of adjustment, a failing roof position switch, a cable that has come off its track or a weak package-shelf motor can confuse the system so it stops to protect itself.
issues.next: Don't force the roof. Close it using the manual procedure in the owner's manual so the car is weather-tight, then have a shop that knows SC 430 roofs read the body codes with a Lexus scan tool. Hinge adjustment or a single switch is often the fix; a full hinge assembly is a much bigger repair.

issues.t: Hard thud when the transmission downshifts
issues.sym: A clunk or thud as the car slows and the automatic shifts down, sometimes appearing suddenly at higher mileage.
issues.why: Shift quality depends on the transmission's control unit and its internal clutches and valves. Owners have been told either the control unit or the transmission itself was at fault, and one replaced the transmission without curing it.
issues.next: Have the transmission fluid and stored codes checked first, and ask about software updates or adaptive resets before agreeing to a transmission swap. Get a second opinion on any large quote.

issues.t: Throttle body fault puts car in limp mode
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on and the car loses power, going into a low-speed limp-home mode.
issues.why: An electrical contact in the electronic throttle body motor could fail. Lexus ran a special service campaign (3LF) to inspect and replace the throttle body on affected cars.
issues.next: Ask a Lexus dealer to check your VIN for campaign 3LF. If the work was never done, have the throttle body inspected and replaced.

issues.t: Water pump leak and timing belt due
issues.sym: Coolant drips or crust near the front of the engine, a sweet coolant smell, or a whine from the front of the engine.
issues.why: Both the SC 300's inline-6 and the SC 400's V8 use a timing belt, and the water pump runs behind it. Owners recommend replacing the belt, pump, seals and idlers together around 90,000 miles or if records are missing.
issues.next: If there are no records of a timing belt change, plan one now along with the water pump and seals. A broken belt leaves you stranded and a leaking pump can overheat the engine.

issues.t: Automatic transmission or torque converter failing
issues.sym: Slipping, flare between gears, shuddering, or overdrive that stops working.
issues.why: Owners link torque converter and overdrive failures in these older SCs to transmission fluid that was rarely changed, letting worn clutches and contaminated fluid damage the internals.
issues.next: Check the fluid color and smell. If it is dark or burnt, have a transmission shop diagnose it before doing a big flush, which can sometimes make a worn unit slip more.

issues.t: Run-flat tires wear out fast and ride harshly
issues.sym: A stiff, jittery ride over bumps, tire noise, and tires that need replacing far sooner than expected, sometimes around 20,000 miles.
issues.why: The SC 430 came from the factory on run-flat tires with very stiff sidewalls so it could be driven after a puncture without a spare. These tires wear quickly and can't always be repaired.
issues.next: Check tread depth and pressures often and keep the alignment in spec. Many owners switch to regular tires and carry a repair kit or roadside plan instead; the tire pressure sensors still work either way.

issues.t: Car pulls to one side or won't hold an alignment
issues.sym: The car drifts left or right on a straight road, the steering wheel sits off center, or the alignment goes out again soon after being set.
issues.why: Lexus issued bulletins on pull complaints and on checking the front ball joints for this car. Worn bushings or ball joints, and the very stiff run-flat tires, make it hard for the alignment to stay put.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked for worn ball joints and bushings before paying for another alignment. Rotating or replacing uneven tires can also cure a pull.

issues.t: Worn front control arm bushings
issues.sym: Squeaks, creaks or clunks from the front over bumps, vague steering, or a shake through the wheel at highway speeds.
issues.why: The rubber bushings in the front control arms dry out and crack with age, letting the arms move more than they should.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected on a lift. Bushings can sometimes be pressed in alone, but many owners replace the complete control arms.

issues.t: Worn engine and transmission mounts
issues.sym: More vibration at idle, especially in Drive, and a clunk when accelerating, shifting or letting off the gas.
issues.why: The rubber and fluid-filled mounts that hold the engine and transmission break down with age and heat.
issues.next: Have a shop watch the engine while a helper shifts between Drive and Reverse. Replace mounts that are torn or collapsed.

issues.t: Power steering pump leaks onto the alternator
issues.sym: Power steering fluid level drops, fluid drips under the front of the car, and the steering may whine. Left alone, the alternator can fail.
issues.why: A seal in the power steering pump wears out. Because the pump sits above the alternator, the leaking fluid soaks it and its wiring.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for wetness around the pump. Reseal or replace the pump soon, and inspect the alternator for fluid damage at the same time.

issues.t: White smoke on start-up from power steering air valve
issues.sym: A puff of white smoke at start-up, or on acceleration in bad cases, and power steering fluid going missing with no visible leak.
issues.why: The power steering air control valve, which raises idle when you turn the wheel, has internal rubber seals that harden with age. Fluid then gets drawn into the intake and burned.
issues.next: Check whether the power steering reservoir is dropping. Replacing the air control valve is a simple repair; burning fluid can foul spark plugs and the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Engine computer capacitors leak, causing stalling
issues.sym: Intermittent loss of throttle or stalling, odd idle, a throttle position code such as P0121, or a scan tool that can't talk to the engine computer.
issues.why: The engine computers of this era use small electrolytic capacitors that dry out or leak with age, corroding the circuit board.
issues.next: Have a shop check the engine computer and its wiring harness. Rebuilt computers with new capacitors are available as an alternative to a new unit.

issues.t: Rough idle when stopped in Drive
issues.sym: The engine shakes or idles unevenly while you are stopped at a light with the shifter in Drive.
issues.why: Lexus issued a bulletin (01304) for rough idle in gear on this model year; the dealer repair follows that bulletin.
issues.next: Ask a Lexus dealer to check whether bulletin 01304 applies. Rule out worn engine mounts, which also make the idle feel rough in gear.

issues.t: Trunk lock won't open
issues.sym: The trunk won't unlock or open with the button, remote or key.
issues.why: Lexus issued a bulletin for an inoperative rear luggage lock on this year. Owners also list a trunk that won't open as a common SC 430 complaint.
issues.next: Make sure the roof is fully closed or fully stowed, since the trunk is locked out mid-cycle. If it still won't open, have the latch and its wiring checked.

issues.t: Rattles from the hardtop rear glass, door trim or mirror
issues.sym: A tick or rattle from around the folding roof's rear glass frame, a buzz from the wood trim on the doors, or the inside mirror shaking so the view blurs.
issues.why: Lexus issued separate bulletins for this model year covering the hardtop rear glass frame (00503), the door wood trim panels (00204/NV00803) and the inside mirror (00304).
issues.next: Note exactly where the noise comes from and ask a Lexus dealer or experienced shop to apply the matching bulletin. Cleaning and treating the roof seals can also quiet squeaks.

issues.t: Creak or tick from the top or bottom of the windshield
issues.sym: A creak, tick or rattle that seems to come from the top or base of the windshield, often on rough roads or when the body flexes.
issues.why: Small stoppers bonded to the top of the windshield and retainers along its lower edge can loosen or rub. Convertibles flex more, so these noises show up readily.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to follow Lexus bulletin L-SB-0090-08, which re-secures the stoppers and retainers. It isn't a safety issue but is easy to fix.

issues.t: Musty or sour smell from the A/C
issues.sym: An unpleasant musty or sour smell from the vents, usually strongest when the A/C first starts.
issues.why: Moisture and debris in the A/C evaporator box and a dirty cabin filter let mold and bacteria grow. Water getting into the car through roof or body seals makes it worse.
issues.next: Replace the cabin air filter and have the A/C drain checked. A shop can clean the evaporator; if carpets are damp, find and fix the water leak first.

issues.t: Squealing serpentine belt
issues.sym: A squeal or chirp from the engine bay at start-up, when the A/C kicks on, or when turning the wheel.
issues.why: The accessory drive belt glazes or stretches with age, and its tensioner or idler pulleys can wear. Lexus issued a bulletin for belt noise, and owners list it as a common SC 430 annoyance.
issues.next: Have the belt, tensioner and pulleys inspected. A new belt is a routine fix; replace the tensioner too if it is weak or noisy.

issues.t: Foggy or hazy headlights
issues.sym: Dim headlights, a cloudy outer lens, or moisture and haze inside the lamp.
issues.why: Plastic lenses yellow and haze from sun exposure, and cracked or poorly sealed housings let damp air inside, where it condenses.
issues.next: Polishing restores a hazy outer lens. If water is inside the lamp, the housing is cracked or the seal has failed and the headlight usually needs replacing.

issues.t: Mark Levinson stereo cuts out or volume jumps
issues.sym: The premium stereo goes silent, crackles, or the volume suddenly jumps to maximum on its own.
issues.why: Owners of SC 430s with the Mark Levinson system report the amplifier or speakers failing with age; it is one of the most reported SC 430 problems.
issues.next: Turn the volume down before starting the car until it is fixed. A car audio shop can test the amplifier and speakers; rebuilt amplifiers are an option instead of new.

issues.t: Gauge needles or climate and radio displays go dark
issues.sym: Gauge needles stop lighting up, or the climate control and radio displays go dim or blank in spots, making them hard to read at night.
issues.why: Small backlight bulbs burn out and the aging circuit boards in the gauge cluster and displays wear out.
issues.next: Bulbs can be replaced yourself if you're comfortable removing panels. Specialist shops can rebuild gauge clusters and displays if the board itself has failed.

issues.t: Doors sag from worn hinges
issues.sym: The door drops when opened, clunks or has to be lifted to latch, and may rub the body.
issues.why: The SC's long, heavy doors use double-jointed hinges whose pivots wear over time, especially if people lean on an open door.
issues.next: Have the hinges checked for play. Worn hinges are replaced individually; avoid leaning on or hanging from open doors.
